notes: Both agree that three-way epistasis findings showing cytoplasmic background can alter nuclear epistasis are well-supported. High overlap (80%) with shared claims C38, C44, C50, C83. LLM includes C22 which is not in peer review grouping.

Both address organellar genome sequencing (C28, C29, C30). LLM finds methodology sound and enrichment significant. Peer reviewers find analysis incomplete, requesting more detail on coding variants and comparison between organellar and nuclear genomes.

Both address comparative variance analysis (C27, C39, C41). LLM finds statistical methods appropriate and conclusions well-supported. Peer reviewers express confusion about heritability analysis methodology and question the fairness of comparing complete cytoplasmic genome to individual nuclear loci.

Both address recommendations for future studies (C51, C52). LLM finds recommendations logical. Peer reviewers agree in principle but express concerns about generalizability to other phenotypes and evolutionary significance, requesting more circumspect claims.

Both address center of phenotype analysis and cytonuclear epistasis (C36, C37, C43). Agreement that epistatic interactions are convincingly demonstrated. LLM emphasizes novel visualization; peer review focuses on substantiation of epistatic interactions.

Both address epistatic network analysis (C33, C34, C35). Agreement that cytoplasmic variation as central hub with extensive epistatic interactions is well-supported. Peer review includes additional claims C36, C37, C42, C43 in their grouping.

Minimal overlap (C70 only). LLM supports claim that effects span central and specialized metabolism. Peer reviewers criticize lack of consideration of existing knowledge about organellar biosynthesis and request analysis of whether organelle-made metabolites are more affected.

Both address background literature context (C1, C2, C11). Agreement that contextual claims about field's focus on nuclear genomes and previous impressions of small cytoplasmic effects are appropriate. LLM covers broader literature review (C1-C12); peer review focuses on subset.
Limited overlap (C45 only). LLM addresses study limitations acknowledgment. Peer review addresses metabolic pathway analysis concerns. Different focus areas with minimal claim overlap.

Minimal overlap (C85 only). LLM supports overarching conclusions about cytoplasmic role. Peer reviewers express concerns about generalizability and evolutionary significance, requesting more circumspect claims.

Both address main conclusions (C49, C84). Agreement that cytoplasmic genetic variation plays central role in metabolomic variation. Peer review explicitly states findings are 'important, and well substantiated.'
Both address epistatic network findings (C21, C82). Agreement that cytoplasmic variation as network hub is convincingly demonstrated as part of substantial epistatic interactions.

Both address comparative effects (C40, C80). Agreement on core finding that cytoplasmic factors have measurable effects. Peer review R1 focuses on overall substantiation; LLM R2 addresses specific variance comparisons.
Minimal overlap (C42 only). Both support claims about cytonuclear epistasis explaining substantial variance. Agreement on epistatic interaction findings.

Both address experimental design and main findings (C19, C20). Agreement that core empirical findings about cytoplasmic effects on metabolites are well-substantiated. LLM R1 covers broader claim set (14 claims); peer R1 focuses on main conclusions.
